composition.serve_who: This sheet (GMMS 108'-118a "AFT COMPANION WAY") is the wiring diagram for the aft companion way hatch — an inflatable/pneumatic hatch-seal (gasket) system with hydraulic-style hatch open/close indication, lock function, an inflate/deflate valve pair, and a remote receiver. The engineer mapping table explicitly maps "AFT COMPANION WAY" -> 575-pneumatic-system, matching the ENGINEER-CONFIRMED MAPPINGS list (same node used for SALOON COMPANION WAY). All functions on this sheet (hatch open/closed indication, digital pressure switch, SW19 open/closed/lock switch, inflate/deflate valves V1 and AUX, reed switch closed signal, FWD remote receiver commanding open/lock/closed/boom light) serve this single pneumatic companionway seal system. The J/BOX terminal strip (2-25) and relay bank Re1-Re8 are the distribution/control infrastructure inside this same J/BOX enclosure, feeding the companionway's own devices — not a separate system, since the sheet titles the whole enclosure as belonging to AFT COMPANION WAY under one J/BOX.

functions.label: Hatch position indication (S1 HATCH OPEN / S2 HATCH CLOSED)
functions.what_it_does: Two indicator devices (S1, S2) show whether the aft companion-way hatch is open or closed, wired from terminals near the J/BOX into the AFT COMPANION WAY control loop.

flow_scenarios.path: J/BOX terminal strip -> incoming wire (left, off-sheet source not traced) -> S1 (HATCH OPEN indicator) / S2 (HATCH CLOSED indicator)

functions.dry_data: Indicator symbols wired via terminals; feed/return side not fully traced on this sheet.

functions.label: Digital pressure switch — inflation status
functions.what_it_does: A digital pressure switch monitors the inflatable hatch seal and opens its contact when the seal is fully inflated, feeding that status back into the J/BOX terminal block.

flow_scenarios.path: pressure switch contact closed -> signal present at terminal block
pressure switch contact opens (per label 'open when inflated') -> signal removed at terminal block -> ground/earth return shown on sheet

functions.dry_data: Two-wire pressure switch with grounded reference; exact pressure setpoint not printed on this sheet.

functions.label: SW19 local open/closed/lock pushbutton panel
functions.what_it_does: A 6-pin pushbutton panel (SW19) lets a local operator command open, closed, or lock states for the hatch seal, each pushbutton pair (contact + return) wired into the J/BOX terminal strip 6-16.

flow_scenarios.path: SW19 pin1 (open button) -> J/BOX terminal -> internal relay/terminal routing -> valve/lock actuation (downstream not fully traced past terminal strip)
SW19 pin3 (closed button) -> J/BOX terminal -> internal routing
SW19 pin5 (LOCK button) -> J/BOX terminal -> internal routing

functions.dry_data: Ground/earth reference below panel; 2.7K resistor/gauge tags on adjacent terminals 12-16 (value legible but role as pull-up/sense resistor vs wire-gauge tag is ambiguous).

functions.label: Inside-locker inflate/deflate pushbutton
functions.what_it_does: A 2-pin local pushbutton inside the locker lets a technician manually command inflate/deflate of the hatch seal.

flow_scenarios.path: SW/ (inside locker) pins 1-2 -> J/BOX terminal block -> routes toward V1/AUX inflate-deflate valves (via internal wiring, terminals 21-23)

functions.label: SW/ BOOM LTS / COCKPIT LTS / C22 switch
functions.what_it_does: A local switch panel on this sheet also carries the BOOM LTS/COCKPIT LTS/C22 circuit through terminal 22, which on the netlist ties directly to V1 valve's return side — i.e. this switch's C22 tap is wired onto the V1 inflate/deflate valve return, not a separate lighting circuit drawn fully on this sheet.

flow_scenarios.path: SW/ (BOOM LTS/COCKPIT LTS/C22) -> terminal 22 -> V1 valve return conductor (net246/433 tie)

key_components: SW/ switch (BOOM LTS/COCKPIT LTS/C22 labeled rows)
functions.dry_data: 3-position switch group with ground/earth reference; BOOM LTS and COCKPIT LTS themselves are lighting circuits detailed on other sheets (690-lts-boom, per acronym mapping) — cross-reference only.

functions.label: V1 — main inflate/deflate valve
functions.what_it_does: V1 is the primary pneumatic valve that inflates or deflates the hatch seal gasket, energised via J/BOX terminals 21/22.

flow_scenarios.path: V1 -> terminal 21 and terminal 22 -> terminal 22 continues to SW/ (BOOM LTS/COCKPIT LTS/C22) switch
NOT TRACED on this sheet — incoming supply conductor to V1/terminals 21-22 dead-ends off-sheet

functions.label: AUX inflate/deflate valve
functions.what_it_does: A secondary/auxiliary valve provides a backup inflate/deflate path for the hatch seal, wired via terminal 23.

flow_scenarios.path: AUX valve -> terminal 23
NOT TRACED on this sheet

functions.label: Reed switch — closed signal feedback
functions.what_it_does: A reed switch provides a 'hatch closed' confirmation signal back into the control loop via terminal 24.

flow_scenarios.path: Reed switch -> terminal 24 -> CLOSED SIGNAL label
NOT TRACED on this sheet

functions.dry_data: Terminal 25 shows a ground/earth stub — a resolved negative-bus return, not an untraced side.

functions.label: FWD Remote Receiver #1 — remote open/lock/closed/boom-light command
functions.what_it_does: A remote-control receiver (FWD REMOTE RECEIVER #1) provides wireless commands for open, lock, closed, and boom-light functions, feeding the same J/BOX terminal strip (17-20) as the local SW19/SW/ switches, and drawing +24V supply and COM return through terminals 6/7 (fused terminal 19 per builtin-fuse note).

flow_scenarios.path: FWD REMOTE RECEIVER #1 pin1 (open) -> J/BOX terminal 17 -> internal routing toward hatch open function
FWD REMOTE RECEIVER #1 pin2 (LOCK) -> J/BOX terminal 18 -> internal routing
FWD REMOTE RECEIVER #1 pin3 (closed) -> J/BOX terminal 19 (fused terminal) -> internal routing
FWD REMOTE RECEIVER #1 pin4 (BOOM LIGHT) -> J/BOX terminal 20 -> onward to boom lighting circuit (cross-reference, not detailed here)
FWD REMOTE RECEIVER #1 pin6 (+24V SUPPLY) and pin7 (COM) tie into J/BOX terminal strip (net466: pins 6=7 tied to SW/ ) — supply source upstream of this sheet not traced

functions.label: Link to PEDESTAL J/BOX 3
functions.what_it_does: Terminals feed a 5-wire link labeled 'to PEDESTAL J/BOX 3' which continues the hatch/lock/closed status signals to another junction box detailed on a different drawing.

flow_scenarios.path: J/BOX terminals (1-5 group near digital pressure switch region) -> to PEDESTAL J/BOX 3 (see DWG 124d)

functions.dry_data: Terminal strip 1-5 dedicated to this cross-link.

infrastructure.system_name: AFT COMPANION WAY J/BOX distribution (relay bank Re1-Re8 + terminal strips 2-25)
facts: Incoming feed: SALOON COMPANION WAY circuit via breaker Q25 6A, arriving at J/BOX terminal 1.
Relay group Re1-Re5 sits in the upper J/BOX section, driven from terminal 1 feed and switch contacts, distributing to terminal strip 2-16.
Relay group Re6-Re8 sits in the lower J/BOX section, distributing to terminal strip 17-25 which feeds V1, AUX valve, and reed switch.
Terminal 19 has a built-in replaceable fuse (fused terminal, per engineer rule on fused-terminal symbol) — carries the FWD REMOTE RECEIVER #1 closed-command line.
2.7K tags on conductors to terminals 12-14 and 16 — ambiguous whether resistor value or wire-gauge callout; not resolved on this sheet.
F6 160A fuse and +24V SERVICE BAT. feed shown at far bottom-left, upstream of Q25 6A breaker — vessel DC service battery supply entering this branch.

uncertainties: Positive/feed side of S1 (HATCH OPEN) and S2 (HATCH CLOSED) indicators is not traced on this sheet — only the outgoing wire toward each device is drawn; the incoming supply/command source is off-sheet or illegible.

Positive/feed side of V1, AUX inflate/deflate valve, and the reed switch (closed signal) is not traced on this sheet — only the return/terminal side (21/22, 23, 24) is drawn; the supply conductor enters from the left and dead-ends off-sheet.

The role of the SW/ (BOOM LTS/COCKPIT LTS/C22) switch is ambiguous: its C22 terminal ties on the netlist directly to V1 valve's return conductor, suggesting this switch may double as part of the V1 circuit rather than being purely a lighting selector — needs engineer confirmation of actual function of this switch relative to V1.
